paper.overview: Combining standard Backpressure (MaxWeight) scheduling with a Last-In-First-Out (LIFO) buffer discipline achieves time-average utility within $O(1/V)$ of optimal while cutting the average delay of all but an $O(1/V^{\log V})$ fraction of traffic from $O(V)$ down to $O([\log V]^2)$ under general finite-state Markovian dynamics—without requiring prior traffic statistics.
paper.hero_blurb: Under LIFO-Backpressure ($V \ge 1$), all but an $O(1/V^{\log V})$ fraction of arriving packets depart with average delay at most $[2D + 2K(\log V)^2 + 2\delta_{\max} + 1]/\tilde{\lambda}_j = O([\log V]^2)$.

theorem:little1.title: Modified Little's Theorem for LIFO Systems
theorem:little1.paper_loc: Section VI-B (L515–534); proof in Appendix A (L1019–1080)
theorem:little1.summary: In a Last-In-First-Out (LIFO) queue, packets stuck near the bottom of the buffer can wait forever—yet packets arriving into a bounded band of slots near the top don't have to! This theorem proves a sample-path version of Little's Law for just those packets that *actually depart* from a finite set of buffer positions $\mathcal{B}$: as long as arrivals into $\mathcal{B}$ occur at rate at least $\lambda_{\min} > 0$ and infinitely many jobs eventually leave, the long-run average delay of departing jobs is at most $|\mathcal{B}| / \lambda_{\min}$. Remarkably, the bound depends only on the *width* $|\mathcal{B}|$ of the active slot band, not on the huge base backlog sitting underneath it.
theorem:little1.sketch: Fix any good sample path where both hypotheses hold. Because each buffer slot holds at most one job at a time, the total time all departing jobs combined spend inside any single slot up to time $t$ cannot exceed $t$; summing over all $|\mathcal{B}|$ slots bounds total departing delay by $|\mathcal{B}|\cdot t$. Meanwhile, at time $t$ at most $|\mathcal{B}|$ arrived jobs can still be sitting in $\mathcal{B}$, so departures satisfy $D(t) \ge N(t) - |\mathcal{B}|$. Dividing the delay upper bound by $D(t)$ and taking $\limsup_{t\to\infty}$ immediately gives $|\mathcal{B}| / \lambda_{\min}$.
theorem:little1.paper_statement: Suppose there is a constant $\lambda_{\min} > 0$ such that with probability 1, $\liminf_{t\to\infty} \frac{N(t)}{t} \ge \lambda_{\min}$, and further suppose $\lim_{t\to\infty} D(t) = \infty$ with probability 1. Then the average delay $\overline{W}$ of departing jobs from $\mathcal{B}$ satisfies $$\overline{W} \triangleq \limsup_{t\to\infty} \frac{1}{D(t)}\sum_{i=1}^{D(t)} W_i \le \frac{|\mathcal{B}|}{\lambda_{\min}}.$$
theorem:little1.witness_note: Section VI-A 2-slot LIFO queue witness with fair-coin probability measure.
theorem:little1.fidelity_summary: All 7 obligations align (1 minor reading: discrete slotted time matching Section III rather than Appendix A's continuous integral).

theorem:qla-markovian.title: [O(1/V), O(V)] Utility-Delay Tradeoff Under Markovian Dynamics
theorem:qla-markovian.proof_origin: Companion paper arXiv:1008.0200v1 (proved from scratch via Poisson route)
theorem:qla-markovian.summary: Standard Backpressure (MaxWeight) routing and scheduling doesn't care whether you serve packets FIFO or LIFO—the queue *sizes* evolve identically. This theorem guarantees that even when network channels and traffic states evolve as a correlated finite-state Markov chain $S(t)$ (not just i.i.d.), tuning the single control knob $V \ge 1$ pushes average operating cost within $O(1/V)$ of the best possible stable policy—including clairvoyant policies—while keeping average total queue backlog bounded by $O(V)$.
theorem:qla-markovian.sketch: While the companion paper [17] uses variable renewal return times and Carathéodory strong duality, our Lean formalization takes a cleaner, self-contained route: we prove finite-state irreducibility and aperiodicity imply Doeblin $L^1$ geometric mixing (`Routine/MarkovMixing.lean`), solve Poisson's equation for the state-dependent dual function, and telescope a perturbed quadratic Lyapunov function $L(t) + h(q(t), S(t))$. Pairing this with a 10-line elementary weak-duality inequality yields both $O(V)$ stability and $f^*_{av} + O(1/V)$ optimality uniformly in $V \ge 1$.
theorem:qla-markovian.paper_statement: Suppose $S(t)$ is a finite-state irreducible and aperiodic Markov chain and the $\eta$-slackness condition (2) holds. Then Backpressure (with either FIFO or LIFO) achieves $$f_{av}^{BP} = f_{av}^* + O(1/V), \qquad \overline{q}^{BP} = O(V),$$ where $f_{av}^{BP}$ and $\overline{q}^{BP}$ are the expected time-average cost and backlog under Backpressure.
theorem:qla-markovian.witness_note: 2-action stochastic network model verifying slackness, Backpressure rule, and stability.
theorem:qla-markovian.fidelity_summary: Lean proves MORE (non-causal optCost benchmark), narrows cost to f ∈ [0, δ_max], and uses an alternative Poisson-equation proof route.
theorem:qla-markovian.route_note: The paper cites companion [17] (variable renewal return times + Carathéodory strong duality), whereas Lean proves the exact same Theorem 2 via **Doeblin $L^1$ mixing + Poisson's equation + elementary weak duality**. Because of this, the companion paper's renewal-time proof is *not* step-checked—while co-authors gain a shorter, self-contained alternative proof.

thm:prob_multi_con.title: Exponential Attraction of Queue Backlogs to the Dual Optimum
thm:prob_multi_con.proof_origin: Companion paper arXiv:0904.3795v1 (proved from scratch in Lean)
thm:prob_multi_con.summary: Theorem 2 says Backpressure queues sit at height $\Theta(V)$, which sounds terrible for delay—unless the queues stay tightly clustered around a single point! Theorem 3 proves that when the dual objective has a unique, sharply peaked ("polyhedral") optimum $\boldsymbol{\gamma}_V^*$, the queue vector is **exponentially attracted** to $\boldsymbol{\gamma}_V^*$: the fraction of time *any* queue wanders more than distance $D + Km$ away from $\gamma_{Vj}^*$ decays exponentially fast as $c^* e^{-m}$, with constants $D, K, c^*$ completely independent of $V$.
thm:prob_multi_con.sketch: Because Backpressure choices form a subgradient of the state-wise dual function $g_{S(t)}$, the squared Euclidean distance $\|q(t) - \gamma_V^*\|^2$ drifts downward whenever we average over a $V$-independent mixing window $T_\nu$ (from Doeblin mixing in `Routine/MarkovMixing.lean`). Combined with the polyhedral dual slope $L > 0$, Euclidean distance $Y(t) = \|q(t) - \gamma_V^*\|$ enjoys strict linear negative drift $-\eta_d$ outside a constant radius $D$. Applying a Padé exponential bound (`Routine/BackpressureDrift.lean`) to $e^{w\max(Y(t)-D,0)}$ and telescoping yields a uniform exponential moment bound $c^*$, from which Markov's inequality produces $c^* e^{-m}$.
thm:prob_multi_con.paper_statement: Suppose $\boldsymbol{\gamma}_V^*$ is unique, $\eta$-slackness (2) holds, and $g(\boldsymbol{\gamma}_V^*) \ge g(\boldsymbol{\gamma}) + L\|\boldsymbol{\gamma}_V^* - \boldsymbol{\gamma}\|$ for all $\boldsymbol{\gamma} \succeq 0$ ($L > 0$ independent of $V$). Then there exist $V$-independent constants $D, K, c^* = \Theta(1)$ such that for any $m \in \mathbb{R}_+$, $$\mathcal{P}^{(r)}(D, Km) \triangleq \limsup_{t\to\infty}\frac{1}{t}\sum_{\tau=0}^{t-1} \Pr\{\exists j,\, |q_j(\tau) - \gamma_{Vj}^*| > D + Km\} \le c^* e^{-m}.$$
thm:prob_multi_con.witness_note: 2-action model verifying unique dual optimum $\gamma_V^*$ and polyhedral slope $L > 0$.
thm:prob_multi_con.fidelity_summary: Lean adds explicit V ≥ 1 (omitted from Theorem 3's box) and narrows cost to f ∈ [0, δ_max]; all other 7 obligations match.

thm:qlalifo_delay.title: LIFO-Backpressure Throughput Fraction and O([log V]^2) Delay Bound
thm:qlalifo_delay.proof_origin: Main paper (Section VI-C) · Composed from Theorems 1, 2 & 3
thm:qlalifo_delay.summary: This is the paper's headline payoff: combine Backpressure's $O(1/V)$-optimal utility with a **LIFO** buffer discipline. Because Theorem 3 traps the queue inside a narrow $O([\log V]^2)$ band $\mathcal{B}_j$ around $\gamma_{Vj}^*$ almost all the time, LIFO serves almost every newly arriving packet from the top of the stack before it ever sinks into the $\Theta(V)$ base backlog. Consequently, all but a tiny $O(1/V^{\log V})$ fraction of packets eventually depart with average delay just $O([\log V]^2)$—an exponential delay improvement over FIFO's $O(V)$, with zero loss in utility!
thm:qlalifo_delay.sketch: Theorem 4 directly composes Theorems 1, 2, and 3. First, finite average backlog from Theorem 2 plus Fatou's lemma ensures only finitely many packets ever get stranded forever, so the never-departing arrival rate is zero. Second, setting $m = (\log V)^2$ in Theorem 3 and invoking Dominated Convergence (using a.s.-constant arrival rates) bounds the out-of-window arrival rate by $\delta_{\max} c^* / V^{\log V}$, proving Part (a). Finally, when $\tilde{\lambda}_j > 0$, packets arriving inside $\mathcal{B}_j$ occupy an enlarged integer buffer band $\tilde{\mathcal{B}}_j$ of width at most $2D + 2K(\log V)^2 + 2\delta_{\max} + 1$ under Eq. (3); plugging this finite band into Theorem 1 immediately delivers the $O([\log V]^2)$ delay bound in Part (b).
thm:qlalifo_delay.paper_statement: Under $V \ge 1$, unique $\boldsymbol{\gamma}_V^*$, $\eta$-slackness (2), and polyhedral growth (15), for any queue $j$ with arrival rate $\lambda_j > 0$, under LIFO-Backpressure: **(a)** the rate $\tilde{\lambda}_j$ of packets arriving while $q_j(t) \in \mathcal{B}_j$ that eventually depart satisfies $\lambda_j \ge \tilde{\lambda}_j \ge [\lambda_j - \delta_{\max} c^* / V^{\log V}]^+$; **(b)** their average delay is at most $W_{\mathrm{bound}} \triangleq [2D + 2K(\log V)^2 + \delta_{\max}] / \tilde{\lambda}_j$ *(formalized with explicit $\tilde{\lambda}_j > 0$ guard and exact Eq. (3) numerator $+ 2\delta_{\max} + 1$)*.
thm:qlalifo_delay.witness_note: Full non-degenerate LIFO packet witness satisfying the guarded $0 < \tilde{\lambda}_j$ hypothesis.
